page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU cache configuration consists of a 32 KB L1 data cache, a 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 33 MB L3 cache. It supports hardware instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES cryptography, and FMA. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.g5ne.xlarge demonstrates entry-level performance characteristics. CPU benchmarks, including stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, place the instance in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests show similar limitations, with read-only large block bandwidth falling into the bottom 10% and write bandwidth in the bottom 25%. Computational tasks like gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench image and text processing consistently score in the bottom 10%. The instance also shows lower-tier results in database operations and static web serving throughput, both registering in the bottom 10% of benchmarks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g5ne.xlarge offers dedicated CPU resources and a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio without the premium cost of high-performance compute or memory-optimized hardware classes. However, the tradeoff is its lower performance-per-resource profile across processing and memory-intensive tasks. Given these characteristics, the instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high computational throughput. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, small-scale development or testing environments, and low-volume background task processing.
